subtitulo: The four hand movements that make your Spanish land in a taxi, at reception and at the market
cena: The porter has already loaded your case into the trunk and is waiting, hand on the open door, for one word he can actually use.

steps.pt: This isn't accent removal — it's a four-move repair kit: equal taps, flat palm, one punch, a finger flick.
Five stable vowels. Keep your palm level; if it tilts, the vowel moved.
English hides weak vowels; Spanish keeps them all. Tap each syllable evenly, then punch the stressed one: cho-co-LA-te.
I want chocolate. Four clean syllables in chocolate; no swallowed ending.

steps.promptPt: At a market counter, point to the chocolate and say what you want. Four equal taps and one punch on LA. Speak now.

steps.pt: Hotel is the trap. English stresses HO; Spanish stresses TEL. One short punch at the end: ho-TEL, then stop.

steps.es: Al hotel del Centro Histórico, por favor.
steps.pinyin: ahl oh-TEL del SEN-troh ees-TOH-ree-koh, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: To the hotel in the Historic Centre, please.
steps.tts: Al hotel del Centro Histórico, por favor.

steps.promptPt: The authorised taxi driver asks where you are going. Give the destination and punch the end of ho-TEL. Speak now.
steps.es: Al hotel del Centro Histórico, por favor.
steps.pinyin: ahl oh-TEL del SEN-troh ees-TOH-ree-koh, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: To the hotel in the Historic Centre, please.

steps.promptPt: The driver checks whether you want the main entrance. Confirm and thank him. Keep the S in gracias: Mexican Spanish does not use the Spanish th here. Speak now.

steps.pt: That S matters here. Gracias, cinco and zapato all use S — the central-Spain th doesn't apply. LL and Y share one sound: start with the Y in yes.
Good afternoon. How can I help you?

steps.promptPt: At hotel reception, the clerk asks how she can help. Say that you have a reservation. Keep every syllable in reservación and punch the final syllable. Speak now.
The clerk asks under what name. Say: under the name Morgan. Do not add an English R after the final vowel. Speak now.

steps.es: Al hotel del Centro Histórico, por favor. Sí, gracias. Tengo una reservación.
steps.pinyin: ahl oh-TEL del SEN-troh ees-TOH-ree-koh, por fah-BOR. see, GRAH-syahs. TEN-goh OO-nah reh-sehr-bah-SYOHN
steps.pt: Shadow the three lines that carry you from the airport into the hotel.
steps.tts: Al hotel del Centro Histórico, por favor. Sí, gracias. Tengo una reservación.

steps.pt: B01 complete. Equal taps, flat palm, one punch, quick flick — you used all four today, taxi to hotel desk.

aprofundar.titulo: The Mexican sound model used in this course

secoes.titulo: S, Z and soft C converge
secoes.corpo: Mexican Spanish is seseante: gracias, cinco and zapato use /s/. Do not import the th model from central Spain. This is a destination choice, not a simplified learner option.
Keep a, e, i, o and u stable, and give each word one clear stressed syllable. Accent marks override the default stress rules.

secoes.titulo: LL and Y share a lane
secoes.corpo: The Mexican model in this course is yeísta. For an English-speaking beginner, the Y in yes is the safe starting anchor. Regional realisations belong in receptive training later, not in your first production drill.

A weak trill is not a travel emergency. Stable vowels, preserved syllables and correct stress buy more intelligibility than performing a regional accent. The target is understood first time, not mistaken for a local.

permissao: You are allowed to sound foreign. A weak trill on the R is not a travel emergency, and nobody is grading your accent. Five steady vowels and one clean punch per word is the whole ask on day one — the flicked R and the soft LL are bonuses you can tidy up any time before you fly.
espelho: Dropping a weak vowel is invisible in English — 'chocolate' loses a syllable, 'probably' becomes 'prob'ly', and nobody blinks, because everyone does it. In Mexican Spanish that same habit removes a syllable the listener is expecting, and a word they own — chocolate, hotel — stops being recognisable as their word.
frasePiso: Five steady vowels, every syllable paid, one punch per word: you may sound foreign and still be understood the first time.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You say a word you both own — hotel, chocolate — and the person in front of you pauses and asks you to repeat it.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: My Spanish is so bad that even the easy words fail, or they didn't hear me.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The word already belongs to Mexican Spanish too, and recognising it is exactly what makes an English speaker speed up and swallow a syllable or move the stress — so it arrives as a word the listener does not have, not as a mispronunciation of one they do.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Say it again slightly slower, one tap per syllable, one punch on the stressed one: ho-TEL, cho-co-LA-te.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The words you already recognise — and there are dozens of them between the airport and the hotel — stop being the ones that fail first.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not with staff at an international arrivals desk or a hotel that serves mostly foreign guests, where the listener decodes accented Spanish all day and will get you on the first try regardless.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Mexican Spanish does not use the central-Spain th sound: gracias, cinco and zapato are all said with a plain S.
fatosDatados.fonte: Academia Mexicana de la Lengua, consulta “Diferencia entre s y z” — na América não se realiza a distinção /s/ × /θ/ (docs/pesquisa-mexico.md §B01).

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Mexican Spanish is yeísta (LL and Y share one sound) and keeps a stable five-vowel system, unlike English's sliding vowels.
fatosDatados.fonte: Academia Mexicana de la Lengua, Lengua oficial, cap. “El español mexicano” (José G. Moreno de Alba) — sistema de cinco vogais; espanhol mexicano seseante e yeísta (docs/pesquisa-mexico.md §B01).

fatosDatados.afirmacao: A single tap of the tongue (pero) is a complete, native Mexican R; the rolled version (perro) is not required for a learner to be understood.
fatosDatados.fonte: CEPE-UNAM, “Retos de la pronunciación del español de México” — descrição pedagógica de tap e vibrante no espanhol mexicano (docs/pesquisa-mexico.md §B01).
